documents.title: Office Order
documents.text: All government officials are requested to submit their weekly progress reports by Friday afternoon. The report must be typed clearly in English and submitted to the section officer. Any delay in submission will be noted in the annual confidential report. This order is effective immediately from the date of issuance by the Ministry of Public Administration.

documents.title: Notice for Typing Test
documents.text: The Bangladesh Public Service Commission will hold a typing test for the post of computer operator next month. Candidates must have a typing speed of at least thirty words per minute in English. The test will be conducted on a standard computer keyboard. No extra time will be given for any technical difficulty. Admit cards must be shown at the entry.

documents.title: Office Memorandum
documents.text: It is hereby informed that all files must be typed and maintained in both Bengali and English versions. The senior assistant will check the accuracy of each typed document before final approval. Typing errors in official letters cause unnecessary delays in administrative work. All staff are advised to practice typing regularly to improve their office efficiency.

documents.title: Circular from Ministry
documents.text: The Ministry of Establishment has issued a new circular regarding the promotion of computer operators. Only those who have passed the departmental typing examination will be considered for promotion. The typing test includes both English and Bengali sections. Candidates must secure at least eighty percent accuracy to qualify for the next grade.

documents.title: Duty Order
documents.text: Mr. Kamal Hossain is hereby posted as the assistant computer operator in the accounts section. He will be responsible for typing all vouchers, bills, and monthly statements. His reporting officer will evaluate his typing speed and accuracy every month. This duty order is issued with the approval of the deputy secretary of the finance division.

documents.title: Official Letter
documents.text: Dear Sir, I am writing this letter to request a transfer from the main secretariat to the district office. I have been working as a typist for five years with excellent performance records. My typing speed is forty words per minute with ninety five percent accuracy. I hope you will kindly consider my application for the transfer.

documents.title: Typing Exam Rules
documents.text: Every candidate must follow the rules of the typing examination strictly. No mobile phone or electronic device is allowed inside the examination hall. The computer keyboard will be provided by the exam authority. You cannot bring your own keyboard or mouse. The test duration is exactly three minutes. Any violation will lead to immediate disqualification.

documents.title: Annual Report
documents.text: The annual report of the ministry must be typed and submitted before the end of the financial year. All sections must provide their typed data to the planning cell. The report contains important statistics about government projects. Typing mistakes in numbers or dates can create serious problems in budget planning. Therefore double checking is mandatory.

documents.title: Office Routine
documents.text: The office routine for computer operators starts at nine in the morning. First you must type the daily attendance sheet. Then you will type letters and memos as directed by the section officer. After lunch break you will update the file register. The last hour is for typing practice to improve speed. This routine must be followed every working day.

documents.title: Application for Leave
documents.text: To the secretary of the ministry, I beg to state that I need three days of casual leave starting from Monday. My mother is sick and needs medical care. I have completed all urgent typing work before applying. Senior assistant Mr. Rahman will handle my duties during my absence. I hope you will grant me this leave kindly.

documents.title: Meeting Minutes
documents.text: The monthly meeting of the computer operators was held on the fifteenth of this month. The chairman discussed the importance of error free typing in government correspondence. It was decided that every operator must practice typing for one hour daily. A surprise typing test will be conducted next week. All members agreed to follow the new guidelines strictly.

documents.title: Secretariat Instructions
documents.text: Bangladesh Secretariat has issued fresh instructions for all computer operators. Each operator must type at least twenty official letters per day. The letters must follow the standard government format. No abbreviation or short form is allowed in official typing. The quality of typing will be checked by the assistant secretary every Friday. Maintain high standards always.

documents.title: Notification
documents.text: This notification is for all candidates who have applied for the post of data entry operator. The typing examination will be held at the central computer lab on the tenth of next month. You must report at eight in the morning with your original ID card. The test result will be published on the ministry website within seven days.

documents.title: Office Circular
documents.text: It is brought to the notice of all employees that typing errors in official documents are not acceptable. Each document must be checked twice before final printing. The quality control section will return any document with more than two typing mistakes. Repeat offenders will face disciplinary action. This circular is issued with the approval of the joint secretary.

documents.title: Promotion Rules
documents.text: The promotion of typists and computer operators depends on their performance in the departmental examination. The exam includes a practical typing test and a short written test. Candidates need at least thirty five words per minute speed with ninety percent accuracy. Those who fail twice will not be eligible for promotion for the next three years. Prepare well.

documents.title: Confidential Report
documents.text: The annual confidential report of each computer operator is prepared by the section officer. The report includes remarks on typing speed, accuracy, punctuality, and behavior. Any complaint from other sections about typing errors is recorded. To get a good report, you must type all documents correctly on the first attempt. Careless work affects your career badly.

documents.title: Training Program
documents.text: The ministry has arranged a fifteen day typing training program for new computer operators. The training will cover English and Bengali typing on modern keyboards. Professional trainers from the National Computer Training Center will conduct the classes. Attendance is compulsory for all newly appointed staff. After the training, a final examination will be held to assess your improvement.

documents.title: Public Service
documents.text: Government computer operators serve the public by typing various certificates and applications every day. You must type birth certificates, national ID cards, land records, and pension papers carefully. A single typing mistake can cause serious trouble for a citizen. Therefore you must treat every document with respect and attention. Your service is valuable for the nation.

documents.title: Speed Test Guidelines
documents.text: In the typing speed test for government jobs, you will be given a passage to type. The passage will be about office administration or public service. You must type exactly what is shown on the screen. No change in spelling or punctuation is allowed. The timer starts automatically when you press the first key. Stop typing when the timer ends.

documents.title: Leave Application Format
documents.text: Every leave application in the ministry must be typed in a standard format. The subject line should clearly state the type of leave. The body should mention the number of days and the reason. You must type your name, designation, and employee ID at the bottom. The application should be addressed to the deputy secretary. Use proper spacing and punctuation.

documents.title: Weekly Report
documents.text: All computer operators must submit their weekly typing report to the administrative officer. The report should include total number of letters typed, number of errors made, and average speed achieved. This data helps the ministry assess the efficiency of each section. Operators with consistently good performance will be rewarded. Submit the report every Saturday before leaving office.

documents.title: Code of Conduct
documents.text: The code of conduct for government typists includes several important rules. You must not share any confidential typed document with outsiders. Typing personal work during office hours is strictly forbidden. You must keep your workstation clean and organized. Any violation of this code will lead to a formal inquiry and possible punishment. Follow the rules strictly.

documents.title: Computer Maintenance
documents.text: Government computer operators are responsible for basic maintenance of their machines. You must keep the keyboard clean and free from dust. The computer should be shut down properly every evening. Any hardware problem should be reported immediately to the IT section. Do not try to repair anything yourself. A well maintained computer helps you type faster without interruptions.

documents.title: Exam Hall Rules
documents.text: On the day of the typing examination, you must enter the hall quietly. Find your assigned computer and sit down. Do not touch the keyboard until the examiner gives the signal. Listen to all instructions carefully before starting. After the test ends, raise your hand and wait. Leave the hall only when permitted. Breaking any rule will disqualify you.

documents.title: Appointment Letter
documents.text: This appointment letter is issued to Mr. Rahim Uddin for the post of computer operator. He has successfully passed the written examination and the typing test. His typing speed was recorded at thirty eight words per minute with ninety two percent accuracy. He is directed to report to the section officer on the first of next month. Congratulations and best wishes.

documents.title: File Management
documents.text: Typing and maintaining official files is a key duty of computer operators. Each file must have a typed cover page with the subject and reference number. All typed documents inside must be arranged in date order. The file register should be updated daily with new entries. Proper file management saves time and helps officers find documents quickly. Be organized.

documents.title: Budget Typing
documents.text: Typing budget related documents requires extra care because numbers are involved. A single digit typed incorrectly can change the entire budget amount. Always double check typed figures against the original document. Use the numeric keypad for faster number entry. Budget documents must be error free before submission to the finance ministry. Accuracy is more important than speed here.

documents.title: Official Seal
documents.text: After typing any official letter, the computer operator must print two copies. One copy is sent to the recipient and the other is kept in the file. The section officer then checks the typed content and applies the official seal. Only after sealing does the letter become valid. Typing errors discovered after sealing cause great embarrassment and waste of time.

documents.title: Daily Register
documents.text: Every government office maintains a daily typing register. The register records which documents were typed, by whom, and at what time. At the end of each day, the senior typist checks the register and signs it. This register is used to measure the workload of each computer operator. Always type your entries in the register clearly and accurately.

documents.title: Transfer Order
documents.text: The following computer operators are hereby transferred to different sections as per administrative requirement. Mr. Hasan from accounts to establishment section. Ms. Fatema from establishment to finance section. All concerned are directed to complete the transfer formalities within seven days. Relieving letters must be typed and signed by the respective section officers. Handover charge properly before leaving.

documents.title: Shortage of Staff
documents.text: The ministry is facing a shortage of skilled computer operators. Many positions remain vacant due to lack of qualified candidates. The typing test results show that most applicants cannot achieve the required speed and accuracy. The ministry has decided to conduct special training programs for potential candidates. Young job seekers are encouraged to practice typing daily to meet government standards.

documents.title: Official Gazette
documents.text: The Bangladesh Gazette is the official government publication. All laws, rules, orders, and notifications are typed and published in the Gazette. Computer operators working in the gazette section must have excellent typing skills. Even a small error in the Gazette can create legal confusion. Therefore only experienced typists with proven accuracy are posted to this section.

documents.title: Inquiry Report
documents.text: The inquiry committee has submitted its typed report regarding the missing file from the records section. The report states that the file was not properly typed or indexed. The computer operator responsible has been identified. He will be asked to explain why disciplinary action should not be taken. This incident shows the importance of careful typing and proper file management.

documents.title: Office Timing
documents.text: The office timing for all computer operators is from nine in the morning to five in the evening. Typing work must be completed within this period. Overtime typing is allowed only with prior permission from the section officer. The attendance register must be typed and signed at the start and end of each day. Late arrival is recorded and affects your annual evaluation.

documents.title: Supply Order
documents.text: A supply order has been typed for fifty new computer keyboards for the typing pool. The order specifies that the keyboards must have standard QWERTY layout with soft keys. Each keyboard will be tested by the computer operators before acceptance. The supplier must deliver within fifteen days. This order is issued by the director of administration and must be followed fully.

documents.title: Warning Letter
documents.text: This warning letter is issued to the computer operator for repeated typing errors in official letters. Despite previous verbal warnings, the quality of work has not improved. The operator is hereby instructed to complete a refresher typing course within one month. Failure to improve will result in a pay cut. A copy of this letter will be placed in the personal file.

documents.title: Advertisement
documents.text: The Ministry of Public Administration invites applications for the post of computer operator. Applicants must have a typing speed of thirty five words per minute in English. A practical typing test will be held at the ministry computer lab. Selected candidates will be posted in different divisions. Application deadline is the thirtieth of next month. No fee is required for this post.

documents.title: Stock Register
documents.text: The computer operator in charge of the store must type and maintain the stock register. All items such as keyboards, mice, printers, and paper must be entered. When any item is issued, the entry must be updated immediately. The stock register is checked every month by the audit team. Typing mistakes in the register cause problems during audit. Be careful.

documents.title: Acknowledgement
documents.text: The computer operator must type an acknowledgement slip for every document received. The slip should include the date, document number, and the name of the sender. A copy is given to the sender and another is kept in the file. This system helps track documents and prevents loss. Always type the acknowledgement clearly so that there is no confusion later.

documents.title: Final Advice
documents.text: To all candidates preparing for the government typing examination, practice daily on a desktop keyboard. Learn the correct finger positions and never look at the keyboard while typing. Focus on accuracy first; speed will come automatically with time. Read each passage carefully before starting to type. Stay calm during the exam and avoid rushing. Best of luck for your future career.
